# ubuntu_command Resource

Manages a command resource via the executor.

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "ubuntu_command" "example" {
  target = var.host
  command = <<-EOT
    echo hello from Terraform
  EOT
  name = "example"
}
```
## Argument Reference

The resource supports the following arguments:

- `allow_destructive_destroy` (Optional, bool) - Explicitly allow destructive destroy for protected or side-effecting host objects managed by this resource.
- `command` (Required, string) - Shell snippet executed during create and update.
- `creates` (Optional, string) - Absolute path that marks the command as already applied when it exists.
- `delete_command` (Optional, string) - Optional shell snippet executed during delete.
- `environment` (Optional, map(string)) - Environment variables exported before the shell snippet runs.
- `interpreter` (Optional, Computed, list(string)) - Interpreter argv prefix. Defaults to ["sh", "-lc"].
- `name` (Required, string) - Logical name used as the Terraform resource identifier.
- `port` (Optional, int64) - Target port for this resource. Overrides provider default_target.port.
- `run_as` (Optional, string) - Execute as this user when the provider resource uses dynamic privilege.
- `target` (Optional, string) - Target host or address for this resource. Overrides provider default_target.target.
- `transport` (Optional, string) - Transport for this resource. The current provider surface supports ssh.
- `triggers` (Optional, map(string)) - Opaque trigger values that can force updates when changed.
- `unless` (Optional, string) - Shell snippet that skips create and marks the resource present when it exits successfully.
- `working_directory` (Optional, string) - Absolute working directory used for command execution.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes:

- `exit_code` (int64) - Exit code from the most recent command execution.
- `id` (string) - Unique identifier for this resource.
- `stderr` (string) - Captured stderr from the most recent command execution.
- `stdout` (string) - Captured stdout from the most recent command execution.
